The register says applicant: "Xiamen Pinnacle Electrical Co.,Ltd"
The document says: "Applicant — BCI INGENIERIA SAS Cra. 88A # 64D-90, Bodega 23 Bogota Colombia"

These are genuinely different company names. "Xiamen Pinnacle Electrical Co.,Ltd" is a Chinese company (Xiamen), while "BCI INGENIERIA SAS" is a Colombian company (Bogota, Colombia). The document text even shows the applicant is BCI INGENIERIA SAS with a Bogota Colombia address, and separately mentions "Manufacturer — Xiam..." (truncated, likely "Xiamen Pinnacle Electrical").

So in the certificate, the applicant is BCI INGENIERIA SAS and the manufacturer is Xiamen Pinnacle Electrical Co., Ltd. The register seems to have conflated the manufacturer with the applicant.

Per the rules: "Genuinely different company or person names = different-entity (best_value = the document's, since the certificate is the legal instrument)."

So verdict: different-entity, best_value: "BCI INGENIERIA SAS".

Note the document value includes an address glued in ("BCI INGENIERIA SAS Cra. 88A # 64D-90, Bogota Colombia") — but the core name is BCI INGENIERIA SAS. Should I consider the address part as document-noise? The rule says "Extraction artifacts (address fragments glued into a name...) = document-noise with best_value from the register." But here the names are genuinely different, so it's not just an artifact issue. The best value should be the clean document name "BCI INGENIERIA SAS" without the address fragment. Hmm, but the rule for document-noise says best_value from register — that applies when it's noise of the same entity. Here it's genuinely different entities, so best_value = document's. I'll use the clean form "BCI INGENIERIA SAS".
